title: How Venting Protects the P-Trap Water Seal
description: A drain trap primary function is to maintain a standing liquid seal that prevents sewer gases from entering living spaces. A common issue occurs when unvented configurations, such as unvented S-traps, create a self-siphoning effect during fixture discharge. As water rushes down an unvented vertical drop, negative pressure pulls the remaining water out of the trap basin, breaking the protective liquid barrier. A properly installed P-trap connected to a code-compliant vent pipe equalizes system pressure, allowing water to drain smoothly while preserving the standing trap seal.

How Venting Protects the P-Trap Water Seal

A drain trap primary function is to maintain a standing liquid seal that prevents sewer gases from entering living spaces. A common issue occurs when unvented configurations, such as unvented S-traps, create a self-siphoning effect during fixture discharge. As water rushes down an unvented vertical drop, negative pressure pulls the remaining water out of the trap basin, breaking the protective liquid barrier. A properly installed P-trap connected to a code-compliant vent pipe equalizes system pressure, allowing water to drain smoothly while preserving the standing trap seal.
